problem_type: Canvas result lifecycle loses durable version order or deletes files before undo history can restore them
symptom: Undo history compaction used relative positions after the journal base moved, so deferred deletion could remain forever or release at the wrong time; legacy numbering must also preserve the durable newest-first sequence.
direct_cause: The closed-project path bypassed the deletion plan with a fallback target, and the V1c eviction test used a mocked store while real updateNode did not create a deletion undo barrier.
class_root: Result identity, durable history order, and physical-file deletion timing were not enforced at their shared lifecycle boundaries.
affected_population: Projects with generated asset files and undo history eviction
Legacy projects whose result pointer differs from history order
Loaded and closed-project deletion entry points
internal_only_reason: The invariant is an application-owned canvas journal and project persistence lifecycle; no third-party behavior decides it.
invariants: A pending file deletion is released only when its absolute journal position is older than the oldest undo/redo-reachable position in the same generation.
Loaded result deletion creates one undo barrier at the shared deletion boundary before store mutation, then records that latest barrier position.
Legacy version numbers follow durable newest-first history order, with newest entry receiving the highest number and oldest receiving 1; a regenerated result continues max+1.

door_reduction.why_not: Deletion has asset-library, node-card, project-close, app-exit, queue, flush, and barrier doors; journal and lifecycle retain independent readers and writers. They converge on the changed shared boundaries but cannot be removed without changing separate user and persistence flows.

generality_proof: Every loaded deletion caller converges on deleteAssetResult, which creates the barrier because updateNode only histories prompt/meta/title/pluginState patches. Closed-project deletion uses the full persisted project plan, so shared references are checked before direct deletion.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Attach pending physical-file deletion to the absolute latest undo barrier and release only records older than the oldest reachable absolute position.
Maintain the absolute journal base offset and report the oldest reachable undo/redo position after compaction.
Normalize legacy result numbers from durable newest-first history order without changing the current pointer payload.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Asset library deletion calls the shared deletion boundary.
Node card deletion calls the same shared boundary.
Project release remains an explicit all-pending flush and does not rely on undo eviction.
App/project close remains an explicit all-pending flush.
All result outcomes converge on nodeRunOutcomePatch; version allocation for new results is an existing forward path outside legacy backfill.

recurrence.reason: The same deletion can be followed by any later gesture until the bounded undo journal evicts its step, and any legacy project can load with a current pointer that differs from history order.
same_class_scan: rg normalizeNodeResultVersionNumbers across canvas snapshot loading
rg deleteAssetResult across asset library and node card entry points

prevention.invariant: Only pending deletions whose absolute journal position is older than the same-generation oldest reachable position are eligible during eviction; explicit close flushes remain comprehensive.
prevention.failure_mode: A pending record without a matching eviction remains queued, and a live reference prevents physical deletion.
prevention.strategy: Use the persisted or live plan as the sole file target authority, create the deletion barrier at the shared boundary before mutation, and use real canvas-store journeys to prove reachability and eviction.

legacy_paths.rationale: The old behaviors are replaced in place at the same shared boundaries; no standalone legacy production path remains.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party dependency controls the lifecycle invariant.

migration: Existing pending records are in-memory only and disappear on restart; closed-project and app-exit explicit flushes remain unchanged. Legacy snapshots are normalized on load without changing result identity or current selection.
residual_risks: A process crash before explicit close cleanup can leave an unreferenced generated file until a future startup cleanup path is added.

invariant_owner_layer.why: Deletion timing is enforced at the pending-file queue boundary; legacy ordering is normalized by the shared lifecycle model and covered by its class tests.
